tex <- function(x) gsub("%", "\\%", x, fixed = TRUE)
# Table caption: trends are in percent per year for contaminants (lognormal),
# in the variable's unit per year for the biological variables (normal);
# for variables measured in %, that is percentage points per year
tab_caption <- function(var) {
  if (var %in% getOption("appendix.normal_vars")) {
    unit <- "the variable's unit per year; percentage points per year for fat and dry weight"
    sub("in percent per year) in mean concentration between start and end",
        paste0("in ", unit, ") in the mean between start and end"),
        sub("in percent per year) in the mean concentration for the last 10 years",
            paste0("in ", unit, ") in the mean for the last 10 years"),
            tabcap, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
  } else {
    tabcap
  }
}
tabcap <- "Parameters: n year all: number of years in time series; n year fit: number years included in analysis; years: sampling time span; p nonlinear: significance of a nonlinear change in the log concentrations over the period; p linear: significance of a linear change in the log concentrations over the period; p overall: significance of a change in the log concentrations over the period; linear change: estimated change (in percent per year) in mean concentration between start and end of the time series; p linear change: the significance of the change; detectable change: the percentage annual increase in concentration that would be detected with 90$\\%$ power using a test at the 5$\\%$ significance level given 10 years of annual monitoring; recent change: estimated change (in percent per year) in the mean concentration for the last 10 years; p recent change: the significance of the recent change; mean last year: the fitted mean concentration in the last year; climit last year: the upper one-sided 95$\\%$ confidence limit on the fitted mean concentration in the last year; threshold: EQS, EAC or other applicable threshold."

#	Statistical treatment

## Data treatment

Time series of contaminant concentrations in biota are assessed by the use of the Harmonized Regional Seas Assessment Tool [@harsat2024]:

The concentrations are log transformed and changes in the log concentrations over time are modelled using linear mixed models. The type of temporal change that is considered depends on the number of years of data:

1-2 years: no model is fitted because there are insufficient data;

3-4 years: concentrations are assumed to be stable over time and the mean log concentration is estimated;

5-6 years: a linear trend in log concentration is fitted;

7+ years: more complex (smooth) patterns of change over time are modelled.

A detailed description of the statistics can be found at: https://dome.ices.dk/ohat/trDocuments/2025/help_methods_biota_contaminants.html

Due to the large number of regression analysis that underlies the statistic results, no formal checks of all statistical model results are done.

## Thresholds
The threshold can be set in a different tissue than that which is analysed within the monitoring programme. The threshold used for evaluation in the report has in these cases been recalculated to represent the corresponding concentration of the threshold in the monitored tissue. EQS used can be found in @HVMFS2019. Choice and tissue conversions of EQS, EAC or other applicable thresholds are explained in @Soerensen2025marine and @Soerensen2025marine.

```{r, results = "asis"}
table_path <- getOption("appendix.thresholds")
if (!is.null(table_path) && file.exists(table_path)){
    raw <- read_csv(table_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

    units <- raw %>%
      slice(1) %>%
      unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>%
      trimws()

    header <- ifelse(units == "" | is.na(units),
                      trimws(names(raw)),
                  paste0("\\shortstack{", trimws(names(raw)), "\\\\", units, "}"))

    thresholds <- raw %>%
      slice(-1) %>%   # drop the units row now that it's folded into the header
      kable("latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
            col.names = header,
            align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "l"),   # Group, Substances, Fish, Mussels, Target
            caption = "Target values") %>%
      kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"))
    note <- getOption("appendix.thresholds_note")
    if (!is.null(note)) {
      thresholds <- footnote(thresholds, general = note, general_title = "",
                             threeparttable = TRUE)
    }
    thresholds
} else
{
  print(paste(table_path, "is missing"))

}
```



# Description of figures and tables

## Figures of spatial variation

### Mean concentration

Spatial visualisation of fitted mean concentrations of contaminants in
{{biota}} biota at the different sampling sites for the latest year.

*Map*: fitted mean concentrations at individual sites visualised by filled circles. The color scale range from light blue (low concentration) to dark blue (high concentration), grey circles indicates that no mean could be fitted. {{spring_note}}If the fitted mean concentration exceeds a threshold, the outer circle is colored red. If the threshold is expressed in a different unit than the
concentration given in the figure, the threshold is recalculated and adjusted to be comparable with the
presented data. The recalculation is based on the mean value (over the entire time series) for e.g. %
lipid weight, or % dry weight in percent for each site.

*Barplot*: fitted mean concentrations visualised by a barplot to allow for quantification and easy comparison between sites. Each bar has the same color as its corresponding circle.

### Trends

Spatial visualisation of estimated trends in  concentrations of contaminants in
{{biota}} biota at the different sampling sites for the last ten years. For quantification of the significance of trends, see the corresponding row in the summary table.

*Map*: trends at individual sites (visualized by filled circles) for the past ten years expressed as the yearly percentage. The color of the circles express the strength of the trend from dark blue (strong negative trend) over white (no trend) to dark red (strong positive trend). {{spring_note}}

*Barplot*: estimated trends (as described above, yearly percentage) visualised by a barplot to allow for quantification and easy comparison between sites. Each bar has the same color as its corresponding circle.


## Summary tables

Statistical summary of the time trends of contaminants in {{biota}} biota for
different sampling sites and species. Consult table captions for detailed information.

## Figures of time series

Time trends of contaminants in {{biota}} biota for sampling sites
and species over the entire sampling period:

*Y-axis units for contaminants*: $ww$: wet weight; $dw$: dry weight; $lw$: lipid weight;

*Data*: Small points represent the measured concentration in an individual or a pooled sample (i.e. one
point equals one observation); Big circular points represents annual geometric mean values; Open blue circles indicate observations under the limit of quantification (LOQ).

*Trend lines*: 1-2 years: no model is fitted because there are insufficient data;
3-4 years: concentrations are assumed to be stable over time and the mean log concentration is estimated;
5-6 years: a linear trend in log concentration is fitted;
7+ years: more complex (smooth) patterns of change over time are modelled.

*Threshold*: indicated by a punctuated line and a green area beneath. Thresholds are recalculated
(expressed in the same unit as the time series data) for substances
where the existing recommended value is expressed in a different unit than the presented data in the
figure. The adjustment is done based on the mean value (for the entire time series at each site) of the
variable used for the recalculation (e.g. $lw$%, $dw$%).
